title: Tableau Peak Concurrency Tracking
dataSources: Tableau logs (`tableau:httpd`, `tableau:vizportal`, `tableau:backgrounder`), REST API, and `workgroup` repository tables via DB Connect.
app: Tableau Server logs via Universal Forwarder; Tableau Server REST API and TSM metrics via HEC; `workgroup` repository via Splunk DB Connect.
spl:
index=bi sourcetype=tableau:httpd
| bin _time span=5m
| stats dc(session_id) as concurrent by _time
| timechart span=1h max(concurrent) as peak_concurrency, avg(concurrent) as avg_concurrency
description: Measures concurrent Tableau sessions in five-minute buckets and rolls the peak up hourly, revealing the load peaks that drive sizing and licensing decisions.
value: Peak concurrency, not average, determines whether Tableau has enough capacity; tracking it prevents peak-hour slowdowns and right-sizes the platform.
implementation: Ingest Tableau session events; schedule hourly and alert when peak concurrency approaches the licensed or engineered limit.
visualization: Timechart of Tableau peak vs. average concurrency.
grandmaExplanation: We watch how many people use Tableau at the same time so it can be sized for the busy periods.
